name: Leviathan
caption: A masked pit-fighter from Singapore who won the World Heavyweight Championship at the fed's own First Night pay-per-view, then defended it against Johnny Detson at Prime Time in North America after exposing a stable's own impersonation scheme.

tenures.source: The fed's own introduction special, "Hype Night" (9 April 1998); its own Public Exercise (19 April 1998); first, second and fourth Sunday Night Madhouse broadcasts (3, 10 and 26 May 1998); Sunday Night Madhouse (28 June 1998); Prime Time in North America (21 July 1998).
tenures.note: Beat Jose Garces at the fed's own first public exhibition (19 April 1998); won a disqualification over Nekrataal (10 May 1998); beat Ares in the tournament quarterfinals (26 May 1998); by the fed's own next surviving broadcast (28 June 1998) was already World Heavyweight Champion, having won the title at the fed's own First Night pay-per-view, which does not survive in the held record. Pinned Mister Dynamic in a non-title handicap match after Johnny Detson refused to defend the title (28 June 1998). At Prime Time in North America (21 July 1998), Superstars, Incorporated tied him up backstage and sent out Jude St. Claire disguised as him to lose the title to Detson in a sham match; the real Leviathan broke free, unmasked St. Claire, and beat the real Detson with the Whirlpool Kick to retain. A man in Leviathan's own mask and costume assaulted Neptune Nitaya backstage (3 May 1998) and later ran down and beat Havoc and Steve Dumars with a limousine and a baseball bat (26 May 1998); Leviathan denied responsibility both times and no document in the held record confirms his identity as the attacker.

name: Lord Pierce Hunter
caption: A haughty English aristocrat who broke Tommy Storm's leg with a chair-assisted submission hold at the fed's own first public exhibition, then advanced through the first round of its World Title Tournament before losing to Neptune Nitaya.

tenures.source: The fed's own introduction special, "Hype Night" (9 April 1998); its own Public Exercise (19 April 1998) and second Sunday Night Madhouse broadcast (10 May 1998).
tenures.note: Beat Tommy Storm at the fed's own first public exhibition (19 April 1998) in a shockingly violent finish, breaking Storm's leg with a chair-assisted ankle lock; lost to Neptune Nitaya in the World Title Tournament's first round (10 May 1998).

name: Prime Time
caption: A flashy Richland, Washington native whose World Title Tournament run ended when "Maniac" John Doe's disqualification loss to him was immediately overturned by a debuting Ares, who beat them both in a handicap match to take the tournament spot.

tenures.source: The fed's own introduction special, "Hype Night" (9 April 1998); its own first and second Sunday Night Madhouse broadcasts (3 and 10 May 1998).
tenures.note: Lost to Paul Kingstead by submission (Ring O' Fire) on the fed's own first house show (3 May 1998); won a disqualification over "Maniac" John Doe in the World Title Tournament's first round after Doe struck the referee with the ring stairs (10 May 1998), then immediately lost the tournament spot in an impromptu handicap match against the debuting Ares.

name: Johnny Detson
caption: A preening Hollywood-billed "Blockbuster" who ducked a World Heavyweight Championship defense, ambushed two number-one contenders to claim the spot for himself, then lost the title match to Leviathan at Prime Time in North America after a failed impersonation scheme.

tenures.source: The fed's own introduction special, "Hype Night" (9 April 1998); its own Public Exercise (19 April 1998); fourth Sunday Night Madhouse broadcast (26 May 1998); Sunday Night Madhouse (28 June 1998); Prime Time in North America (21 July 1998).
tenures.note: Beat Paul Kingstead at the fed's own first public exhibition (19 April 1998) and again in the World Title Tournament quarterfinals (26 May 1998). Had a scheduled World Heavyweight Championship defense against Leviathan postponed to Prime Time in North America, sending Mister Dynamic in his place for a non-title handicap loss instead (28 June 1998); the same night, ambushed number-one-contender hopefuls Marshall Duncan and Ares with the rest of Superstars, Incorporated and falsely declared himself the new number-one contender. Lost the World Heavyweight Championship match to Leviathan at Prime Time in North America (21 July 1998) after teammate Jude St. Claire's disguise as Leviathan was exposed.

name: Alec Donaven
caption: A determined Scotsman who beat "Maniac" John Doe at the fed's own first public exhibition, then beat the much larger Zero Gonzalez on the fed's own first house show.

tenures.note: Beat "Maniac" John Doe at the fed's own first public exhibition (19 April 1998); beat Zero "El Nino" Gonzalez with a DDT (the Donaven Drop) on the fed's own first house show (3 May 1998), despite Gonzalez no-selling most of the match.

name: Jerome Turner
caption: "Mister Intimidation," a Toronto-billed powerhouse who won a brutal Falls Count Anywhere match against Peter Hand on the fed's own first house show, driving him through a hot-dog stand.

tenures.note: Won a Falls Count Anywhere match over "Naturally Gifted" Peter Hand by ten-count knockout on the fed's own first house show (3 May 1998), after the brawl left the ring, the sound booth and the parking lot, ending with Hand driven through a hot-dog stand.

name: Jose Garces
caption: "El Hombre Del Toro," a high-flying cruiserweight from Pamplona who won the CWC International People's Championship and retained it at Prime Time in North America despite a guardrail powerbomb and masked interference.

tenures.source: The fed's own introduction special, "Hype Night" (9 April 1998); its own Public Exercise (19 April 1998) and second Sunday Night Madhouse broadcast (10 May 1998); Sunday Night Madhouse (28 June 1998); Prime Time in North America (21 July 1998).

Wrecking Crew in revenge during the fed's own Boiler Room Rumble (28 June 1998). Retained the title at Prime Time in North America (21 July 1998) when challenger Jude St. Claire won by disqualification after being powerbombed on the guardrail by Romulus and finished off by a masked Mike Sebastian.

name: Rex

name: The Linebacker
caption: One half of the tag team Dragonfire, who beat down Paul Kingstead on the microphone before later turning on the Hardcore Icons during the Boiler Room Rumble.

name: Anthony Lindsey

name: Jean Watts
caption: The CWC's founding president, a six-foot brunette introduced at the fed's own first press conference who doubles as its ring announcer and, on occasion, its most dangerous in-ring hand.

tenures.note: Founded the CWC alongside a four-man board of directors; announced both an International People's Championship tournament and a cross-promotional card with the World Wrestling Organization, War of the Ages, for 16 June 1998, which the held record shows the CWC won. Announced three Summerstorm matches and a title defense (28 June 1998); ruled the World Tag Team Championship match at Prime Time in North America a no-disqualification bout mid-match, and was blocked by Kim and Monique from taking the newly-won tag titles at ringside (21 July 1998).

name: Andrew Holden

name: "Playboy" Jude St. Claire
caption: Superstars, Incorporated's wealthy "Playboy," a First Night International People's Championship semifinalist who fought Jose Garces for the title and impersonated Leviathan in a botched attempt to steal the World Heavyweight Championship.

tenures.source: The fed's own Sunday Night Madhouse broadcast, 28 June 1998
tenures.note: Hijacked a number-one-contender match between Marshall Duncan and Ares to instead broadcast Superstars, Incorporated's own backstage ambush of both men, then falsely declared pins for Johnny Detson (28 June 1998). Lost to Jose Garces for the International People's Championship by disqualification after masked interference (Prime Time in North America, 21 July 1998) -- the title did not change hands. Disguised himself as Leviathan and "lost" the World Heavyweight Championship to Johnny Detson in a sham match after Superstars, Incorporated tied up the real champion backstage; unmasked and beaten by the real Leviathan when the fraud was exposed (same broadcast).

tenures.note: Escorted Jude St. Claire to the ring alongside Mister Dynamic and powerbombed Jose Garces on the security railing during St. Claire's International People's Championship match; ambushed and handcuffed to the railing by a masked fan wearing a "Sacrificer" Nekrataal t-shirt, whose identity was never confirmed.
